national_articles.headline: Bharti Airtel shares rise up to 2% after telco hikes tariff on postpaid plans
national_articles.body: Market Mastery Find the weak links Shares of Bharti Airtel rose over 2% to an intraday high of Rs 1,854.7 apiece on October 7 after the company announced a price hike of Rs 50 on its postpaid plans, effective immediately. The company also launched a new postpaid plan that provides free roaming for one international trip each year along with all other existing benefits. The new plan comes into force from Thursday. The plan can be activated at any time of the customer's choice for a period of five days. In August, the telecommunications major had added 2.1 million subscribers as compared to 2.7 million added in July, as per data from the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India. On October 7,Bharti Airtel sharesclosed trading 1.5% higher at Rs 1,837.8 apiece. Bharti Airtel has raised its postpaid tariffs by Rs 50 with a revamped set of plans that bundle one free international roaming trip every year. The new plans come into effect on October 8, 2026, and existing postpaid subscribers will be moved to the nearest higher plan within a month, company sources told PTI on Wednesday. A company source said the free international roaming offer is worth Rs 2,000, reported PTI. In effect, the revamped plans mean a Rs 50 hike over current tariffs for postpaid. In a release, Airtel announced "the launch of new postpaid plans, with even more benefits built in". "From October 8, 2026, customers can enjoy one international trip with free roaming every year with these new postpaid plans, along with all existing benefits," the release said. The complimentary roaming pack includes 5 GB of data, 60 minutes of calls, 25 outgoing SMS and free incoming SMS, valid for five days. Customers can activate the pack whenever they choose. On family plans, every member is eligible for the free roaming benefit. "Free international roaming is the latest addition to Airtel Postpaid plans, which come with a superior experience through fast lane technology, unlimited data, and network-level protection against spam and fraudulent links.  "Customers can also enjoy a range of entertainment subscriptions and access to exclusive experiences through the Airtel Postpaid Advantage Club, including comedy shows, movie premieres and concerts," the release said.

national_articles.headline: PTC Industries shares rise 7% after company launches QIP
national_articles.body: Shares of PTC Industries, a leading manufacturer of high quality critical and super-critical components and subsystems for aerospace, defence and industrial applications, rose 7% on October 7 after the company launched a QIP (qualified institutional placement). The company is looking to raise up to Rs 1,800 crore ($186 mn), people familiar with the matter told Moneycontrol. Moneycontrol hasrevieweda copy of the deal term sheet of the QIP. The board of directors of the firm authorised the opening of the issue on October 6 and approved Rs 22,150 per share as the floor price of the issue, according to an exchange disclosure. The last closing price of the firm was Rs 23,125 per share. On October 7,PTC Industries sharesclosed 7% higher at Rs 24,770 apiece. “The indicative issue price is Rs 21,060 per share and the QIP proceeds will be used for debt repayment by the company, investment in its subsidiary Aerolloy Technologies for funding working capital requirements and purchase of plant and machineries and investment in step down subsidiary Trac Precision Solutions Limited," said one of the persons cited above. A second person added, “Investment banks ICICI Securities and Goldman Sachs are acting as advisors on the proposed transaction.”  The share price of PTC Industries has moved up by more than 54 per cent in the last six months.

national_articles.headline: Kalyan Jewellers shares jump up to 6% after company says Q2 consolidated sales rose 26% YoY
national_articles.body: Market Mastery Find the weak links Shares ofKalyan Jewellers Indiaclimbed as much as 6% to an intraday high of Rs 581.2 apiece on the NSE on October 7 after the jewellery retailer reported a 26% year-on-year increase in consolidated revenue for the September quarter. Revenue from its India operations grew 27% during the quarter. The company recorded around 20% growth in same-store sales despite a high base, supported by strong Navratri sales in the year-ago period. Kalyan Jewellers was the top gainer in the Nifty 200 index. The stock ended 4% higher at Rs 571 on October 7, with more than 18 million shares changing hands. The traded volume was below the three-month average daily volume of nearly 22 million shares. Revenue from international operations increased around 18% year-on-year, while revenue from West Asia rose 12%, driven by same-store sales growth. International markets accounted for 11% of the company's overall revenue mix, according to an exchange filing. Revenue from lifestyle jewellery brand Candere jumped 64% year-on-year during the quarter. Kalyan Jewellers added 11 Kalyan stores and nine Candere showrooms in India on a net basis, along with one showroom in the UK. The company also launched its first regional brand, Akshaya Thanga Maligai, in Chennai and plans to open four stores under the brand during the current financial year. Meanwhile, shares of Titan Company fell 4% after the company released its September quarter business update after market hours on Tuesday. Global brokerage JPMorgan subsequently lowered its target price on the stock, taking a cautious view of its near-term performance. Titan shares ended 4% lower at Rs 4,365 on October 7, making it the worst-performing stock in the Nifty 50. The company's consumer business revenue rose 25% year-on-year in the September quarter, led by international operations. Revenue from the jewellery segment increased 21% year-on-year, driven by strong growth at Caratlane. Revenue at Caratlane rose 32%, while the combined revenue of Tanishq, Mia, Zoya and beYon increased 20% year-on-year. JPMorgan reduced its target price on Titan by nearly 2% to Rs 5,540. The brokerage expects the stock to face near-term pressure after the company's September quarter revenue came in below its estimates, although it noted that the product mix could provide support to margins.  According to JPMorgan, the next major catalyst for Titan's share price will be its September quarter earnings. Investors will also track management commentary on festive demand, initiatives to expand the buyer base amid volatile gold prices, and the company's margin performance and outlook.

national_articles.headline: Rupee ends at five-month low at Rs 96.78 per dollar after RBI shifts stance to ‘calibrated tightening’
national_articles.body: Market Mastery Find the weak links The rupee ended at a near five-month low on October 7 after the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) shifted its policy stance to ‘calibrated tightening’ from ‘neutral’, a move that caught market participants by surprise. The local currency closed at Rs 96.78 per dollar, compared with the previous close of Rs 96.43. The rupee opened marginally higher at Rs 96.45 but fell as much as Rs 96.83 during the day, moving closer to its record low of Rs 96.98 per dollar. The currency emerged as Asia’s worst-performing unit for the day despite the rate hike and the relatively hawkish stance adopted by the central bank. Some traders said the RBI was present in the spot market around the Rs 96.55-per-dollar level to prevent a sharper depreciation in the currency and keep it from breaching a fresh record low. The central bank has been regularly intervening in the market over the past two weeks to prevent the rupee from weakening beyond the psychologically important Rs 97-per-dollar level. Earlier in the day, the RBI raised the policy rate by 25 basis points to 5.50 percent. Governor Sanjay Malhotra explained that the term ‘calibrated tightening’ was intended to signal a milder form of monetary tightening, indicating that further rate hikes could remain on the table, although the pace may not be as aggressive. “The shift in stance from neutral to calibrated tightening added to nervousness in the currency market, indicating further rate hikes could remain on the table... The rupee is likely to remain under pressure with elevated volatility, with the range seen between Rs 96.45 – Rs 97.25,” Jateen Trivedi, VP Research Analyst - Commodity and Currency, LKP Securities, said.  At the post-policy press conference, Malhotra said the rupee was undervalued based on indicators such as the real effective exchange rate (REER), and that financial markets could sometimes be irrational.

international_articles.headline: ‘Even your father can't stop us’: Sohail Afridi turns up heat on Shehbaz govt, challenges Islamabad over Imran Khan’s release
international_articles.body: Market Mastery Find the weak links Pakistan's political confrontation is moving closer to a direct showdown in Islamabad, with Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi challenging the federal government to stop the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf's march. In an exclusive interview with CNN-News18, Afridi also accused Pakistan's courts and authorities of disregarding orders concerning meetings with jailed former prime minister Imran Khan and his medical treatment. As the PTI convoy advances towards the capital, the dispute has widened from Khan's imprisonment to questions over judicial orders and the federal government's handling of the protest. ‘No one can stop us from reaching Islamabad’ Afridi has thrown down a direct challenge to the Shehbaz Sharif government as the PTI's long march continues towards Islamabad. Speaking exclusively to CNN-News18, the KP chief minister said the march would be called off if even one of the party's seven demands was found to violate the Constitution or the law. “I challenge the whole of Pakistan. I challenge the entire world that out of those seven points, if even a single demand is proven to be unconstitutional or illegal, then at that very moment, I will cancel my long march," Afridi said. The PTI's seven demands include the release of Imran Khan and issues linked to the treatment and access of the jailed former prime minister. Afridi also issued an unusually blunt warning to those attempting to prevent the protesters from reaching the federal capital. “When we say that we will reach Islamabad and show you, then forget about you, even your father won’t be able to stop us," he said. His comments come as the federal government has tightened security around Islamabad and warned the protesters against entering the capital. PTI march heads towards capital amid standoff The long march began from Gandi Chowk in Lakki Marwat on October 4, with Afridi announcing that he would personally lead the movement. The convoy subsequently travelled through southern parts of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa before reaching the Mattani area on the outskirts of Peshawar on October 6. The march follows failed talks between the PTI and the federal government. Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi has accused Afridi of undermining the negotiations, while the PTI has maintained that its demands concerning Khan and other political issues remain unresolved. With the convoy moving towards Islamabad, the federal government has deployed security personnel and warned that protesters would not be allowed to force their way into the capital. Afridi, however, has continued to insist that the march will proceed. Afridi accuses courts of ignoring orders on Imran Khan The KP chief minister also used the CNN-News18 interview to question Pakistan's judicial system over the implementation of court orders concerning Khan. Afridi claimed that orders relating to his access to the PTI founder had not been implemented. “Kohat residents, the chief justice of Pakistan is from your city, yet my hearing hasn’t taken place," he said. “I told the chief justice of the Islamabad High Court, but he didn’t even respond to my greeting." He further alleged that a three-judge high court bench had ordered that he be allowed to meet Khan, but that the directive was not acted upon. “An order comes from three high court judges that I should be allowed to meet my leader, but it isn’t implemented," Afridi said. Afridi also raised the issue of Khan's medical treatment and alleged that a Supreme Court directive concerning his treatment had similarly not been implemented. “An order comes from three Supreme Court judges that Imran Khan’s treatment should be carried out at Shifa International Hospital in Islamabad, but it isn’t implemented," he said. Dispute over Khan’s medical treatment The issue of Khan's medical care has become another point of confrontation between the PTI and the federal authorities. According to the PTI's account, Pakistan's Supreme Court had ordered Khan's transfer to Shifa International Hospital in Islamabad in August. He was instead taken to the government-run Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences before being returned to prison. The federal government subsequently sought a review of the Supreme Court order. The dispute has since become part of the PTI's wider argument that decisions concerning Khan are not being implemented despite judicial intervention. Afridi has now made the alleged non-implementation of these orders part of his broader criticism of the federal government and Pakistan's institutions. Afridi launches personal attack on government leader The KP chief minister also used the interview to launch a personal attack on an unnamed government leader. “That coward who has lost his election against an elderly woman. If this shameless person’s father had been a man, he wouldn’t have sat on the seat of an elderly woman," Afridi said. “I know about your lack of honour, and I also know about the honour of that coward who is your leader," he added. The remarks came as Afridi continued to reject calls for the PTI to abandon its march towards Islamabad. Islamabad prepares for confrontation The latest escalation comes as the federal government faces a direct challenge from the PTI-led provincial administration in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. The federal authorities have warned against attempts to enter Islamabad, while the PTI has insisted that the march will continue until its demands are addressed. For Afridi, the immediate objective remains the federal capital. “No one can stop us from reaching Islamabad," he said.  With the PTI convoy moving closer to Islamabad and security restrictions tightening around the capital, the standoff between the Shehbaz Sharif government and the PTI-led KP administration is now entering a more confrontational phase.

international_articles.headline: ‘Israel’s decline accelerated after Oct 7’: Iran military chief's fresh claim as Israelis mark 3 years since Hamas attack
international_articles.body: The Hamas attack of October 7, 2023 has accelerated Israel's decline, the chief of staff for Iran's armed forces said Wednesday, as Israelis marked the third anniversary of the deadliest day in their country's history.  "The Resistance Front turned its defensive strategy into an offensive strategy for the legitimate defence of the Palestinian people and their land, and accelerated the decline of the Zionist regime," Ali Abdollahi said in a statement.

international_articles.headline: Two lethal injections, still alive: Christa Pike survives execution attempt. What went wrong and what happens next?
international_articles.body: Market Mastery Find the weak links Christa Pike was supposed to become the first woman executed by Tennessee in more than two centuries. Instead, the September 30 execution attempt ended with the 50-year-old still alive after two doses of pentobarbital were administered. Pike was taken to hospital and placed on a ventilator, with her lawyers initially saying she was critically ill. Nearly a week later, her legal team says she is conscious, awake and speaking. The failed execution has now triggered an independent review and fresh questions over Tennessee's lethal-injection process. Christa Pike is awake and speaking after failed execution Pike's lawyers said on Tuesday that she had regained consciousness and was able to speak, marking a significant change from the condition reported immediately after the failed execution. Randall Spivey, one of Pike's attorneys who witnessed the execution attempt, said: “Christa is alive right now. We don’t have a sense of her prognosis or much update on her health at the moment, but we do know that she is alive right now," Al Jazeera reported. Pike had been taken to a Nashville hospital after the execution attempt and was placed on a ventilator. Her lawyers said doctors worked to remove the pentobarbital from her system. She sustained serious injuries to her arms, including burns and blisters, and remains under medical care. Her attorneys are now seeking information about what happened inside the execution chamber and have urged Tennessee Governor Bill Lee to commute her death sentence to life imprisonment. They have described the experience as “chemical torture”. What happened inside the execution chamber? Pike's execution was scheduled for September 30 at Riverbend Maximum Security Institution in Nashville. She had been sentenced to death for the 1995 killing of 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer, a fellow student at the Knoxville Job Corps. Pike was 18 at the time of the killing. After the US Supreme Court allowed the execution to proceed, Tennessee officials administered two doses of pentobarbital, the drug used under the state's single-drug lethal-injection protocol. But the procedure did not result in Pike's death. According to witnesses cited by the Associated Press, Pike remained alive after the injections. AP journalist Kim Chandler, who was among the media witnesses, described what happened after the execution chamber blinds were closed. “The blinds were closed for the first time to the execution chamber at 7:46 pm (23:46 GMT); they opened again at 7:49 pm (23:49 GMT). Her mouth fell open a few times, and she began to loudly snore. She gasped a few times,” Chandler said, as quoted by Al Jazeera. Pike could still be heard breathing and snoring after the drugs had been administered. Emergency vehicles eventually arrived and she was transported to hospital. Tennessee's Department of Correction said it had followed the state's established execution protocol. However, the department did not initially explain why the procedure failed. Why did the lethal injection fail? The precise cause remains under investigation. One possibility raised by experts is a problem with intravenous access. AP reported that medical experts believe the IV line may have malfunctioned, potentially allowing the drug to enter surrounding tissue rather than the bloodstream. Pike's lawyers have also pointed to difficulties involving the IV access. Another possibility raised in media interviews concerns the condition of the drugs. Stafford Smith, a lawyer who has witnessed numerous executions, suggested that an ineffective or improperly handled drug batch could be one explanation. “The first is that the drugs were probably out of date. Something that we’ve been observing a lot for the last 10 years is that they administer drugs that are no longer valid,” Smith said, according to the publication cited in the original report. He also pointed to the difficulty of establishing intravenous access. “The other thing about Pike is that, as is very common with people who end up in her situation, they’ve been through a lot of abuse and drug abuse. So it might have been very hard to find her veins and get a needle into it." “Moreover, doctors are also not allowed to take part in this process in the US. So they have incompetent people administering such drugs, which could have resulted in the injection failing,” Smith added, according to the publication. Those explanations remain allegations or possible causes, rather than established findings. Tennessee has ordered an independent investigation into the failure. Why did Tennessee halt further executions? The failed procedure has prompted Governor Bill Lee to suspend the state's remaining scheduled execution for 2026. Lee ordered a “comprehensive, third-party review” to determine what went wrong during Pike's execution attempt. The decision comes after Tennessee faced another execution-related problem earlier this year, when officials were unable to establish the required intravenous access during the attempted execution of Tony Von Carruthers. The latest incident has also prompted lawmakers to examine alternatives to lethal injection. Tennessee Republican leaders said they would consider methods including the electric chair and firing squad if lethal injection is deemed unreliable. What happens to Pike now? Pike's legal status remains unresolved. Her lawyers are seeking to have her death sentence commuted to life imprisonment and are also pursuing access to records and evidence from the failed execution, including information about the drugs and the procedure. The question of whether Tennessee could attempt another execution is also likely to generate further legal challenges. Pike's lawyers have argued that the failed procedure caused significant physical trauma and raised constitutional concerns. For now, however, Pike remains alive and under medical care. The legal battle is also unfolding against the backdrop of the unusual nature of her case. Pike is believed to be the first known person in the United States to survive after receiving a full lethal-injection attempt. What was Pike convicted of? Pike was convicted of murdering Colleen Slemmer in January 1995. According to the case against her, Pike and her boyfriend, Tadaryl Shipp, lured Slemmer into a wooded area near the Knoxville Job Corps, where they attacked her. Prosecutors said Pike regarded Slemmer as a romantic rival. The killing involved extreme violence, including the carving of a pentagram into Slemmer's body. Pike was convicted of first-degree murder in 1996 and sentenced to death. Shipp, who was 17 when the crime occurred, was sentenced to life imprisonment with the possibility of parole. A third teenager involved in the case received probation. Pike's lawyers had argued before her execution that her age at the time of the crime, history of severe sexual abuse and other mitigating circumstances should have been taken into account. A federal appeals court briefly halted the execution on September 30 before the US Supreme Court ultimately allowed it to proceed. The execution then went ahead, but the state failed to carry it through.  Now, with Pike conscious and speaking, Tennessee faces an unprecedented legal and administrative question over what happens next.

international_articles.headline: EU prepares import cap on Chinese hybrid cars to balance trade
international_articles.body: Market Mastery Find the weak links The European Union is preparing so-called safeguard measures that would limit imports of Chinese hybrid vehicles into the bloc in a bid to reduce the trade deficit. The European Commission, which handles trade matters for the EU, may impose the restrictions after Chinese-made hybrid sales surged in Europe, according to people familiar with the matter. They now make up a quarter of total sales, while the growth of imports of Chinese electric vehicles, which already face steep EU tariffs, has slowed. Safeguard measures allow the EU to restrict products from a sector if there’s been a surge of imports into the bloc. One way the commission can enforce this is through the use of tariff-rate quotas, which place a levy on imports above a certain volume. The cap proposed by the EU would be time-limited, the people said. The commission plans to use hybrids as a test case, which, if successful, could be replicated with other sectors where the bloc sees trade imbalances, according to people familiar with the matter. The EU’s trade chief, Maros Sefcovic, will travel to Beijing later this week for talks with Chinese Commerce Minister Wang Wentao, and the bloc’s plans could change depending on how those discussions go, said the people, who spoke on the condition of anonymity. A key aim by the EU would be to keep the cap on hybrids low enough to avoid a retaliatory response from Beijing, said the people. A spokesperson for the commission declined to comment. The EU’s trade deficit with China exceeds €1 billion ($1.1 billion) a day, and the commission has been scrambling to harden its trade policy to defend European sectors falling prey to Chinese imports. EU leaders will meet in mid-October to discuss the situation and possible new instruments they can use to strike back against China’s trade practices. The commission is scheduled to present by the end of the year a series of tools to address the trade imbalance and diversify the bloc’s supply chains. Brussels and Beijing launched negotiations earlier this year, with the EU setting an October deadline to unlock tangible results toward achieving a more balanced trade relationship. In addition to trade and investment, negotiations have also focused on intellectual property rights, World Trade Organization reform and export controls where the bloc is seeking a fast-track application system to speed up China’s supply of critical raw materials. The bloc also wants China to improve access to its market by lowering trade barriers, as well as ease restrictions on goods including brandy, pork, and dairy products. Beijing has so far been open to discussing investments and boosting imports from the EU but has been reluctant to explore ways to tame its own exports. It is unclear whether Beijing will entertain proposals to cap shipments of hybrid vehicles, the people said. China previously opposed earlier talk of a voluntary cap on hybrid car exports. “These so-called voluntary export restrictions seriously violate WTO rules and run counter to the laws of the market economy and the principle of fair competition. China firmly opposes this,” a spokesperson for the Commerce Ministry said in a statement last month. China has asked the EU to loosen its own export controls but the bloc’s executive arm has pushed back against those demands, arguing that the area is a member state competency. Chinese automakers grabbed a record share of Europe’s car market in August, with brands including BYD Co. making up nearly 12% of total new-car sales in the region. They accounted for one in four sales of all hybrids — or one in three for hybrids with a plug. Chinese hybrid vehicles don’t currently face the same steep EU tariffs as electric-vehicle imports from the country. Beijing has pushed to replace those levies with so-called price undertakings, a mechanism to control overall export volumes by setting minimum prices. Earlier this week, France and Germany proposed that the EU develop and adopt a new tool that could restrict access to the bloc’s single market in the event of a trade war. The EU’s two biggest economies also called on the bloc to launch new trade probes in critical areas such as chemicals.  EU ambassadors will be briefed on the outcomes of this week’s meetings on Sunday, the people said.
